subject: Tuck-and-Roll: proposed term transition + burst safeguard
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@brightframe.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightframe.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Term change request + ramp protection questions

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for the overview in the call today. BrightFrame is keen to move off the short-term monthly cadence and land on something that gives our product teams runway. Two asks from procurement and finance: 

1) Move from month-to-month to a 24-month term with a 9-month staged ramp in year one (we'll gradually hit committed capacity).
2) An auto-renew that defaults to annual renewals unless we opt-out 60 days prior.
3) A burst/buffer safeguard — in Q4 we expect spiky load; we want a documented overage/credit approach instead of surprise bills.

High level: we like Redwood and want predictable pricing, but need commitments around co-terming other BrightFrame products (they are on different start dates). Can you sketch how Redwood would handle co-terming multiple contracts into a single renewal cadence and what the pricing trade-offs look like for a multi-year commit?

Attaching a simple internal timeline for our finance team.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Li
VP, Platform Engineering
BrightFrame

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@brightframe.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term change request + ramp protection questions

Sarah — really appreciate the clear asks and the timeline. Quick responses inline and then a next-step proposal: 

1) 24-month term with 9-month staged ramp: feasible. We typically define a staged ramp as committed baseline + milestone gates (months 1–3: 40%, months 4–6: 70%, months 7–9: 100%). We can map credits if actual usage under-indexes versus committed.

2) Auto-renew: we support auto-renew with a 60-day opt-out. For co-termed agreements, auto-renew applies at the consolidated term boundary (so if you co-term product B into product A, the consolidated contract will auto-renew as a single entity).

3) Burst safeguard: propose an overage buffer pool (monthly burst allowance expressed in token-hours) + a capped soft overage rate for spikes. If spikes exceed the buffer, customer can convert excess into temporary burst capacity (charged at pre-agreed uplift) or trigger temporary dedicated burst at a capped rate. We can also offer an escrowed credit to smooth immediate billing risk.

Co-terming approach (brief):
- Option A: Convert ancillary contracts onto the primary term immediately and apply a one-time proration + credit to align start dates.
- Option B: Phase co-terming over a 3-quarter window with stepped credits.

I need to check with Marissa on discounted laddering for a 24-month commit and whether we can front-load onboarding credits to help with Q4 spikes. I've looped Kar (karthik) for pricing mechanics and Marissa for legal/ops.

Proposed next step: we will send a revised quote and a mutual action plan (MAP) by EOD Wednesday with the two co-terming mechanics and a suggested burst buffer construct. If that works, we can schedule a 30-min procurement alignment for Thurs.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: pricing sketch for BrightFrame (24m, ramp, co-term options)

Olga / Karthik — internal note before we return to Sarah. High-level pricing sketches below, please comment: 

- Net effective discount bands for 24-month: 12–15% off list depending on commit size and whether they accept the soft overage cap.
- Ramp recognition: allocate committed tokens as an annual schedule but allow credits to be banked and applied if they underuse during onboarding. Credits expire at month 18 to avoid indefinite liability.
- Co-term Option A (immediate consolidation): prorate remaining months and issue a consolidation credit equal to 50% of the prorated remainder for each ancillary contract we pull in (to make ops simple).
- Co-term Option B (phased): ramp a consolidated term over 3 quarters; offer 1.5% additional discount if they agree to phase and early-pay year 1.

Burst safeguard: offer a 10% monthly burst pool (calculated on expected monthly committed tokens) + a soft overage rate at 1.25x list for all usage above the pool; provide an option for a 90-day escrow credit (prepaid) to convert soft overage into covered burst.

Questions: 1) Legal — any issues with 50% consolidation credit? 2) Karthik, confirm the soft overage 1.25x math and how it shows up in billing statements (we want it on the invoice line, not separate).

Marissa
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
